answer: One identity claims one falcon route, locks a 70-credit bond, and files a velvet tag bound to its key. Three beacon stations record the falcon flight in a window and publish bearings; an auditor triangulates the path from the beacon logs and burns the bond if the path misses the route or a tag repeats. The first filing costs 37 credits, the kth 37+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5032; 1000 fakes pay 2,534,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-flock ring fails: one falcon cannot fly three routes at once. An honest identity pays 37 once and recovers its bond after a clean triangulation.
